summary.text: Andy Pobjoy is the Liberal candidate for Geelong at the 2026 Victorian election. Born and raised in Geelong, he owns and runs the Piano Bar in the city centre and sometimes performs there himself. The party presents him as a small business owner and parent rather than a career politician.

occupation.text: Owner and operator of the Piano Bar, Geelong

priorities.text: Easing the cost of living
Improving community safety
Infrastructure and services to keep pace with Geelong's growth
Backing small businesses and working families
Restoring accountability in Victorian government

sources.title: Geelong: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Andy Pobjoy, Liberal for Geelong, Liberal Victoria

summary.text: Bree Vanderpol is the Victorian Socialists candidate for Geelong at the 2026 Victorian election. The ABC lists Vanderpol's job as surveyor, and on the party's site Vanderpol describes themselves as a minimum-wage worker and a member of the party's Geelong branch. Their campaign focuses on the cost of living, renters and the condition of Geelong's city centre.

priorities.text: Someone has to stand up for the little guy
Bringing down everyday costs such as groceries and housing
Protecting renters from being forced out of their homes
Reviving Geelong's city centre and the privatised Market Square
Opposing One Nation and the influence of large corporations

sources.title: Geelong: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Bree Vanderpol, Victorian Socialists

summary.text: Brenden Grull is standing for Socialist Alliance in Geelong at the 2026 Victorian election. He is a painter and decorator, a union supporter and a father. He has taken part in local campaigns over public housing, the environment and the protection of community and library services.

priorities.text: I want to fight for the rights of people in this community.
Rebuilding the strength of democratic trade unions
Government reinvestment in housing and the public sector
Ending government handouts to the rich and powerful

sources.title: Geelong: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Brenden Grull for Geelong, Socialist Alliance

summary.text: Christine Couzens, listed by Parliament as Chris Couzens, has been the Labor member for Geelong in the Legislative Assembly since 2014. Before that she worked in community development, served as electorate officer to her predecessor Ian Trezise, and held the top two posts at Geelong's Trades Hall Council. She is recontesting Geelong in 2026.

summary.text: Emilie Flynn is the Greens candidate for Geelong at the 2026 Victorian election. A former teacher who lives in Geelong West, she is co-chief executive of Geelong Sustainability, a community climate action group. She ran for the Greens in the federal seat of Corio in 2025 and won 15.9 per cent of first preferences.

occupation.text: Co-chief executive of Geelong Sustainability; former teacher

priorities.text: Climate justice and social justice must go hand in hand
Relief from the rising cost of living and housing pressure
Opposes government support for the Viva Energy gas terminal in Geelong
Secure homes, fair pay and a healthy environment for all

sources.title: Geelong: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Emilie Flynn, Candidate for Geelong, Australian Greens
Candidates of the 2025 Australian federal election, Wikipedia

summary.text: John De Lorenzo is One Nation's candidate for Geelong at the 2026 Victorian election. Originally from Colac, he has spent more than twenty years working in manufacturing and exporting, holds a Deakin University MBA, and has been a non-executive director on the Colac Area Health board for nine years. He contested the federal seat of Corio as an independent in 2025, taking 3.6 per cent of first preferences.

prior_roles.note: The ABC gives nine years on the board but no start year, and doesn't say whether he still serves.

summary.text: Maria Bengtsson is standing for Family First in Geelong at the 2026 Victorian election. Her party page describes her as a Croatian-Swedish immigrant who has spent more than 40 years working in the dental industry, and says she has been married for 44 years, with three adult children and four grandchildren. A Family First candidate of the same name stood for Greenvale at the 2022 state election and for Calwell at the 2025 federal election; the sources don't confirm it is the same person.

summary.text: Pippa Macpherson is the Animal Justice Party candidate for Geelong at the 2026 Victorian election. Her party's page describes her as a qualified chef who has lived in Geelong all her life and plays local football and cricket. She took part in the YMCA's Victorian Youth Parliament in 2026, which the page says led her to stand.

priorities.text: End duck hunting, brumby culling by shooting, and greyhound racing
Stronger protection for native wildlife, including closing loopholes in Authority to Control Wildlife permits
More young people and women in Parliament
Protecting the environment
